INDIA’S SEMICONDUCTOR DEPENDENCY HAS A BIG STORY TO TELL. 🇮🇳

Nearly 49% of India’s imported semiconductor devices come from China.

That’s not just a trade statistic. It’s a reminder of how strategically important semiconductor supply chains have become for India’s technology ambitions.

According to the FY 2025–26 import-origin data highlighted in this graphic:

📊 India’s semiconductor import distribution:

🇨🇳 China – 48.9%
🇸🇬 Singapore – 8.4%
🇮🇩 Indonesia – 7.5%
🇻🇳 Vietnam – 6.6%
🇹🇭 Thailand – 4.7%
🇯🇵 Japan – 3.8%
🌍 Others – 20.1%

What does this mean for India?

1️⃣ Supply-chain diversification is becoming critical.

2️⃣ Domestic semiconductor manufacturing needs stronger momentum.

3️⃣ Chip design, fabrication, packaging and testing capabilities must grow together.

4️⃣ Developing skilled semiconductor engineers is equally important.

India has ambitious semiconductor manufacturing goals, but building a resilient semiconductor ecosystem requires more than setting up fabrication facilities.

It requires technology, infrastructure, investment, talent and long-term strategic planning.

The real question is not whether India will become a semiconductor powerhouse.

It’s how quickly India can reduce critical supply-chain dependencies while building its own capabilities.

At SEMI DESIGN, we believe the next chapter of India’s semiconductor journey will be shaped by technology and talent.

🇮🇳 Designed in India. Developed for the world.

What is your perspective? Can India significantly reduce its semiconductor import dependency over the next decade?

This was my 45th year on planet Earth, and looking back, I'm amazed at how much fit into one trip around the sun. 

3 things that brought me the most joy: 
🧭 FRIENDSHIPS, 
💡LEARNINGS, 
👶🏽👶🏽 and FAMILY EXPANSION in progress!

This week, Blade Runner 2099 premiered on Prime Video. You'll find glimpses of my choreography in it and some incredible Czech performers. Loved working on it with my dear friend Lucie Drábková! …and can’t wait to watch it with my dearest Beata Banikova on my next visit to Prague!!

I became Chair of the Strategic Planning Committee atSpace for Humanity and helped launch the first Citizen Space Agency for Earth. This board of directors is an ongoing source of learning and inspiration for me. 

I continued as Advisor for Human-Centered Design atApptronik - developing humanoid robots and learning from some of the world’s top designers and engineers. I also made my first investment in the company, alongsideCapital Factory, Rockaway Ventures andGoogle. 

With our Moonshot team, we grew our reach from 139 countries to 170 and received 9,700 applications, almost double last year. Each one is a young person ready to change the lives of others for the better. All of this is only possible thanks to our magnificent mentors like Sheila Lirio Marcelo, Yvonne Hao, or carla piñeyro sublett 🤍 and our team led byErin G., events built by Klara Honzikova and community stewarded byMelissa El Feghali, Rok Dolenc and many others. 

This community is definitely a part of my extended family and I am honored to work on it with leaders on our board:Jan Bednar, Chris Varelas, Ranji Nagaswami, Alexander Braun, and Andrea Piana!!!

I traveled to 10 countries and 6 US states to learn from and teach young people about creativity, technology, leadership and changemaking.

🇮🇩 Indonesia, 🇸🇬 Singapore, 🇨🇿 Czech Republic, 🇨🇭 Switzerland, 🇺🇸 New York, 🇮🇹 Italy, 🇬🇧 United Kingdom, 🇺🇸 Massachusetts, 🇺🇸 Illinois, 🇨🇦 Canada, 🇰🇷South Korea, 🇺🇸 Florida, 🇺🇸 California, 🇺🇸 Texas, ...

And the biggest news of all: my partner and I decided to start a family, and life surprised us with twins! 👶🏽👶🏽 We are so excited! To make room for them, we moved to a bigger home, still in Brooklyn, New York.

To everyone who walked beside me this year, from my team and mentors to the young leaders, my friends, my family and my partner: THANK YOU! Here's to orbit 46. 🚀

posts.text:
The fastest way to make a buyer disappear in Southeast Asia is to send them the proposal they needed so URGENTLY.

Buyer: "Can we get the quotation by 5pm? Management wants to review it today."

Me: "Sure, shall we discuss it together tomorrow?"

Buyer: "Just send it first. I'll call you."

- Demo completed.
- Engineers pulled into meetings.
- Special pricing approved.
- Proposal delivered before 5pm.

And then...
Emails? Nothing.
WhatsApp? Two blue ticks.
Calls? Straight to voicemail.

Funny how their internet worked perfectly when they needed the quotation.

Welcome to the ghosting pandemic in Southeast Asian enterprise sales.

To be fair, there's a cultural side to this. In Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand, people may avoid saying NO directly because they don't want to damage a relationship.

I understand that. But I'm perfectly happy hearing:
↳ We don't have the budget.
↳ We're considering another vendor.
↳ Management has changed its priorities.

That's also why, before involving my technical team, I want to establish whether there's an approved project, who makes the decision and when we'll review the proposal together.

If they're simply exploring costs, I'm happy to provide a ballpark figure.

I can respect the culture, give buyers space and make it comfortable for them to decline.

But I'm certainly not committing revenue to the board based on a buyer whose last known words were "Please send quotation ASAP."
--

posts.text:
What Is the Real Value of a WPPE Certificate?
Many people spend significant time, effort, and money to obtain a Wakil Perantara Pedagang Efek (WPPE) certification. It represents their commitment to learning, understanding capital market regulations, and preparing for a professional career in the securities industry.

But what happens after they obtain it?
Some securities companies seem reluctant to provide opportunities for WPPE holders to work in the roles they are qualified for. Instead, they are sometimes offered positions as Introducing Brokers (IBs). Others advertise equity sales positions but impose transaction targets that seem unrealistic, without considering actual market conditions.
The stock market does not always move upward. There are bullish, bearish, and sideways markets. There are also periods when investors prefer to wait rather than trade.

How can companies expect employees to achieve aggressive transaction targets without considering market realities?
Securities companies should also give their employees the opportunity to:
- Serve and maintain relationships with existing clients.
- Provide market insights and investment education.
- Build long-term client trust.
- Develop sustainable AUM and transaction growth.

A securities professional should not be measured solely by transaction volume. They should also be valued for their ability to build relationships, educate investors, and deliver meaningful services.

If securities companies want sustainable growth, they must invest in their people, not simply impose targets.

To all securities companies and hiring managers: there are many WPPE-certified professionals who genuinely want to contribute to Indonesia's capital market.

Give them a fair opportunity to prove their value.
#WPPE #CapitalMarket #SecuritiesIndustry #EquitySales #IndonesianStockMarket
